title: Introduce sampled compliance assertions and deprecation manifest auto-generation
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Automates generation of lightweight compliance assertions from sampled telemetry and emits a deprecation manifest for models flagged for retirement. Adds a release-note hinter that produces concise, verifiable bullets used by automated changelog drafts.
body: Context: Teams onboarding models have asked for faster, auditable signals that justify deprecation and release-note text without pulling full traffic-level telemetry. This PR introduces: 1) a sampled-compliance-anchor extractor that ingests a small, privacy-aware sample of evaluation and production telemetry to synthesize assertion snippets (latency-95, p50 inference time delta, embedding-drift score, license/TOU flags); 2) a deprecation-manifest generator that composes a small machine-readable manifest when a model crosses configurable deprecation thresholds; 3) a release-note hinter that emits human-friendly bullets (one-liners) derived from the anchors for downstream changelog automation. Motivation: reduce manual curation for model retirement notes and provide a reproducible provenance link back to the sampled telemetry used to make the decision. The description below documents the implementation, rollout plan, and verification checklist. Implementation summary: - New pipeline component under registry/services/anchors that subscribes to the sampled-telemetry topic and runs a lightweight rules engine (thresholds + heuristics) to create assertion records; assertions are anchored to a provenance token (sha-like) and retained for 90 days. - Deprecation manifest schema (v1) added to registry/schemas/deprecation_manifest_v1.json; manifests include model_id, candidate_versions, triggers, anchor_ids, suggested-rollback (if applicable), and suggested replacement models. - Small adapter to the changelog draft generator: registry/scripts/release_hint_gen.py reads anchors/manifests and emits one-line hints annotated with provenance tokens and metric deltas. - CLI: registry/bin/manifest-inspect to allow solutions engineers to inspect generated manifests and rerun anchor calculation for a specific model and time window. Rollout plan: start as feature-flagged and opt-in per team for 2 weeks; integrate into the 'retire-model' playbook and surface suggested release-note hints in the onboarding console. Security & privacy: sampling respects dataset redaction rules; no PII stored in anchors. Anchors include aggregated metrics and hashed provenance tokens only. Backfill and migration: small backfill job added (migration/2026-01-sampled-anchors-backfill.py) that samples 72h of recent telemetry for high-usage models; backfill runs under a dedicated queue to avoid impacting serving. Testing & verification: unit tests for rules engine, e2e smoke harness against a synthetic telemetry producer, and manual verification steps documented in the PR checklist. Ops considerations: retention (90 days) configurable; manifests can be revoked if upstream telemetry changes; API endpoints rate-limited to prevent abuse. Related work: builds on previous onboarding telemetry samplers (ENG-2104) and changelog-autodraft infra. Request: review the rules threshold defaults and the deprecation manifest schema before merge.
